answer: An agent economy can require every identity to complete a sequential verifiable delay function before it may act, chaining each output into a public mesa of checkpoints. A delay function cannot be parallelized or bought in bulk, so a farm spinning up a thousand fake identities must wait out a thousand separate slow computations, one per alias, while an honest agent passes a single haven checkpoint in seconds. The pearl is that the delay output itself becomes proof of patience: bound to one key, expiring fast, never reusable, so each new alias pays the full waiting cost again.
